answer: Randomized admission thread. Each epoch, agents join a waitlist; a public verifiable-randomness beacon draws a fixed number of slots, and admitted identities inherit a unique lineage vine linking them to the draw. An attacker cannot precompute which pseudonyms get slots, so mass registration requires committing real work before knowing outcomes. Unused or withdrawn slots return to the lagoon of future draws. Per-identity cost: pre-commitment work on many uncertain candidates, most of which fail the draw.
